title: Three Days and One Short Chart
subtitle: 天气气候 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）
meta: 主题语境：天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）　|　核心词汇：forecast　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 forecast 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1967 the keeper ① issued a forecast that no fisherman in the station would have trusted, and he said the issuing was the whole of the morning. The ② forecast, meaning the prediction itself and not the weather, ran three days and stayed untrusted in the book; a forecast, he said, is the only thing in a station that is judged by how long it is left untrusted.

Every ③ forecast in that station had the same short chart beside it, and the ④ forecast at the far desk, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A forecast, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to trust; the keeper said the trusting is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the forecast was the whole of the matter, meaning the outlook and not the prediction. The ⑥ forecast, meaning the outlook and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody trusts; forecast, he said, is either something you issue or the only word that means both a prediction and an outlook. He said the outlook is the part they remember.

By 1974 the ⑦ forecast had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short chart. The ⑧ forecast of the whole thing, the keeper wrote in September, was one station and three days of trusting; forecast, he said, is either the one at the far desk or the reason you learned to trust. He said the trusting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ forecast I remember is the one trusted in the plan, which closed in 1976 and is still described as the quietest in the station. A ⑩ forecast, my mother said in 1978, is the only one that improves by being trusted; every forecast, she said, is an outlook that has agreed to look like a prediction. She said the outlook was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 预报；预测（指气象站里每一份旁边的那一份）
B. n. 预报（指那一份本身，与天气实况相对）
C. 固定搭配：issue a forecast 发布一份预报
D. n. 预报（指留给孩子们的那一份）
E. n. 预报（抽象总称，指一座气象站的预报之事）
F. n. 预报（指计划里写到、被人信过的那一份）
G. n. 前景；展望（the forecast for，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）
H. n. 展望（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）

answers.why: issue a forecast 意为“发布一份预报”，1967 年那位看守人发布了一份气象站里没有一位渔民肯相信的预报。
forecast 意为“预报”，指那一份本身而不是天气实况，它经过了三天而在簿子上没有人相信。
forecast 意为“预报”，指气象站里每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一张短短的图表。
forecast 意为“预报”，指留给孩子们的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
forecast 意为“前景、展望”，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西，叔叔说这份展望就是那件事的全部。
forecast 意为“展望”，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西而不是那份预报，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
forecast 意为“预报”，指计划里写到、被人信过的那一份，到 1974 年这一份成了计划里的一行。
forecast 意为“预报”，看守人九月写道，整件事的预报之事是一座气象站和三天的相信。
forecast 意为“预报”，我记得的是计划里被人信过的那一份，1976 年结束了，至今仍被说成气象站里最安静的一份。
forecast 为抽象总称，母亲 1978 年说，一份预报是唯一会因为被好好相信而变得更好的东西。
